name: Trajectory Forecasting (GATv2 ST-GNN)
purpose: Predict multi-agent future trajectories from metric track history so the platform can warn before a struck-by event. Owns the spatio-temporal graph attention model, the camera-bound checkpoint contract, the TensorRT/ONNX export path and the offline training script.

public_interfaces.name: WorkZoneSTGNN.forward
public_interfaces.contract: Consumes a graph of metric track windows, returns a 3.0 s horizon per agent with a confidence; runs on CPU when no accelerator is present.

public_interfaces.name: checkpoint contract (camera_fingerprint / validate_checkpoint)
public_interfaces.contract: A forecast checkpoint is only usable with the camera calibration and sampling rate it was trained for; mismatches are refused, not coerced.

public_interfaces.name: ONNX / TensorRT export
public_interfaces.contract: Export is optional and offline; absence of tensorrt must not break the CPU runtime path.

acceptance_criteria: A checkpoint trained for camera A is refused for camera B with a named reason.
Forecast status is reported as AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE on the wire; an absent checkpoint never fabricates a trajectory.
Training is reproducible from reviewed metric trajectory windows only.
Inference keeps the edge cycle inside the documented latency budget on CPU.
risks: Forecast quality is unvalidated against physical-site data; the documentation explicitly labels forecast claims as design targets.
Checkpoint compatibility is a release-coupling point: a new detector or calibration invalidates existing forecast checkpoints.
